items.label: SPY5 + SPYL (S&P 500 duplication)
items.detail: SPY5 ($221,155.21, 288 sh, live get_account_positions) and SPYL ($118,560.00, 6,240 sh) both track the S&P 500 and together total $339,715.21 = 69.80% of NAV ($486,720.80, live get_account_summary). Fresh 1-year daily-return correlation between the two (n=214 aligned trading days -- SPYL's shorter inception plus LSE/NYSE calendar differences narrow the overlap window versus the fuller ~250-day US series, get_price_history closes through 2026-09-02) is +0.9848 -- effectively one position split across two tickers, treated as a single combined position for concentration purposes.
items.recommendation: Trim SPYL (the smaller, more redundant leg, 6,240 shares) by roughly a third (~2,080 shares, ~$39,520 at $19.00) and redeploy into DBC (Invesco DB Commodity Index): this run's fresh correlation test found DBC the single best diversifier against the SPY5+SPYL blend (-0.2427) of seven candidates tested (SHY +0.0019, IEF +0.1210, TLT +0.1408, AGG +0.1794, EFA +0.4739, VWO +0.5463). DBC is itself a volatile, inflation-linked asset, not a low-vol ballast -- size it as a genuine diversifier, not a safety cushion (use the SHY ballast below for that).

items.detail: get_pa_allocation (ESTIMATED -- returned realtime:false, dated 2026-09-01) shows 0% of NAV in bonds by ASSET_CLASS (Commodities 9.65%, Equities 84.37%, Cash 5.98%); live get_account_positions confirms no bond ETF is currently held. CME FedWatch-derived odds of a 25bp September 16 hike now stand at roughly 66.4% as of Sept 1-2, 2026 (sources: Forbes, 'CME FedWatch Provides A 66% Chance Fed Will Hike Rates In September,' Aug 31, 2026; Yahoo Finance gold coverage citing the same 66.4% figure, accessed Sept 3, 2026), essentially unchanged from the prior run's 65-68% read and still sharply up from ~36% pre-Jackson Hole. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks cited PCE inflation at 3.7% (12mo) and 4.1% (6mo), both well above the 2% target.
items.recommendation: Establish a Treasury ballast sized at roughly 5% of NAV (~$24,340) in SHY (1-3Y): SHY showed the lowest correlation to the account's dominant SPY5+SPYL position of any hedge candidate tested this run (+0.0019 of 7 tested) -- the most defensible shock absorber if the Fed surprises hawkish on Sept 16.

Size at roughly 15-20% of the cluster's value (~$3,610-$4,810).

items.label: Iran-conflict energy-shock tail risk -- fresh escalation this week
items.detail: The Iran conflict escalated again this week: fresh US strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz followed attacks on two oil tankers in that shipping route, pushing Brent up roughly 5% to ~$95/bbl on Sept 2, 2026 (up 13.24% over the past month, 40.33% y/y) -- the highest level since late July (source: Al Jazeera, 'Oil prices hit 1-month high as US-Iran attacks dim Strait of Hormuz outlook,' accessed Sept 3, 2026). The account holds no pure-play oil & gas exposure -- CCJ is a uranium miner, not oil & gas -- so direct hit is limited, but a broad equity selloff or inflation surprise (an energy shock complicates the Fed's Sept 16 decision either way) would still pressure SPY5/SPYL (69.80% of NAV).
items.recommendation: No new position needed given minimal direct energy exposure; the DBC hedges recommended above (SPY5+SPYL and materials-satellites clusters) would partially cushion an oil-driven inflation or growth shock. Revisit sizing if Brent sustains above $100/bbl -- it is currently just under that level at ~$95 after this week's escalation, closer to the trigger than in prior runs but not yet past it.
